I've been doing this same rotation for 20 years on this land. My 5 mu grows wheat in winter and then maize on the same ground in summer. That's just how it works here in Quzhou. My husband's brother works in the city now so it's mostly me handling the fields, with help from my husband when he's not doing day labor.

**Wheat (October sowing):** I'll buy the improved Kenong 199 seed like last year from the village supply store — it's reliable and the local extension people recommend it. For fertilizer I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and then urea again at jointing stage in spring, same as always. My neighbor uses about the same amounts I do. With the well I'll water four times: once before winter sets in, once when it greens up in March, once at jointing, once at heading. I'll spray herbicide in late autumn and then do one fungicide spray in spring when powdery mildew shows up. I'll use the rotary tiller after maize harvest to work the stalks in.

**Maize (June, right after wheat harvest):** I'll use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed — most people here do, yields are good. I direct seed it to save time since wheat harvest and maize planting is back-to-back and I'm tired. I put compound fertilizer in at planting and top up with urea at the big bell stage. Summer rains usually help but I'll pump the well once if it gets dry in July or August. I spray once for corn borer and herbicide early on.
